identity.title: Measuring Protoplanetary Disk Gas Surface Density Profiles with ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: early ALMA observations of $^{13}$CO and other lines are publicly available through its Science Verification program

evidence.quote: The exceptional disk around the nearby (122 pc) Herbig Ae star HD 163296 is, fortunately, both big and bright.

question.value: Can gas surface density profiles of protoplanetary disks be measured from 13CO integrated intensity images, and what resolution and sensitivity are needed for T Tauri disks?

evidence.quote: We extend the modeling approach presented in (cite: 2014ApJ...788...59W) to show that gas surface density profiles can be measured from high fidelity $^{13}$CO integrated intensity images.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00010.SV.
fitting ALMA observations of the HD 163296 disk
The same parameters match the C$^{18}$O 2–1 image
early ALMA observations of $^{13}$CO and other lines are publicly available through its Science Verification program

what.value: Gas temperature structure T_gas(R,Z) for HD 163296

evidence.quote: we use the gas temperature structure, $T_{\rm gas}(R,Z)$, described in (cite: 2013ApJ...774...16R)

what.value: Stellar mass 2.3 Msun and inclination 45 deg

evidence.quote: we set the stellar mass, $2.3\,M_\odot$, and inclination, $i=45^\circ$, based on (cite: 2011ApJ...740...84Q)

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Library of 748 RADMC-3D 13CO 2-1 models for HD 163296; 9900-model T Tauri grid used for simulated observations

evidence.quote: We created an image library by running 748 models over the range of parameters shown in Table [1](#tab:HD163296_grid).
The resulting image library consists of 9900 models.

what.value: Modeling methodology (CO isotopologue abundance, molecular layer, temperature parametrization)

evidence.quote: We follow the methodology in Paper I but create a library of resolved images rather than a table of total line luminosities.

unstated_but_needed: Calibration and imaging procedure for the SV data, and how the zero-moment maps were made (channel range, clipping)

method.value: RADMC-3D 13CO 2-1 radiative transfer of azimuthally symmetric Keplerian disks, grid in Mgas, Rc, gamma

evidence.quote: We then calculate the $^{13}$CO 2–1 line emission using the radiative transfer code RADMC-3D.

key_parameters.value: CO freeze-out 20 K; dissociation N_H2 > 1.3e21 cm^-2; 12CO/H2 = 1e-4; 12CO/13CO = 70

evidence.quote: isotopologue ratio, \[$^{12}$CO\]/\[$^{13}$CO\]=70.

assumptions.value: Hydrostatic equilibrium, Keplerian rotation, azimuthal symmetry

evidence.quote: The gas is assumed to be azimuthally symmetric, in hydrostatic equilibrium and under Keplerian rotation.

validation.value: LTE vs NLTE differ by <1 mJy km/s per pixel

evidence.quote: we compared models with LTE and NLTE excitation and found no substantial difference ($<1$ mJy ${\rm km~s^{-1}}$ pixel$^{-1}$).

analysis_steps.goal: Fit HD 163296 zero-moment map with MCMC

method.value: Linear interpolation of image library over parameters, MCMC with flat priors

evidence.quote: The MCMC modeling was run with a flat prior for each parameter over the range shown in Table [1](#tab:HD163296_grid) using the `emcee` software package

fitting.value: emcee, flat priors over grid range; median and 68% intervals

evidence.quote: from which we calculate median and 68% ($\pm 1\sigma$) confidence intervals

validation.value: Interpolated images within 3% of full radiative transfer

evidence.quote: we found that interpolated images averaged within 3% of a full radiative transfer calculation.

method.value: Rerun RADMC-3D with median parameters, vary only CO/C18O abundance by least squares to the zero-moment map

evidence.quote: only varied the \[CO\]/\[C$^{18}$O\] abundance to minimize the least squares difference with the zero-moment map.

findings_qualitative.value: Fits to 12CO 3-2 by earlier work give higher central densities, steeper profiles and smaller outer radii than the 13CO fit

evidence.quote: Both find higher central densities, steeper profiles, and smaller outer disk radii than our fits to $^{13}$CO.

claims.hypothesis: Gas surface density profile parameters can be fit from a 13CO zero-moment map
claims.experiment: MCMC fit of image library to HD 163296 ALMA SV data
claims.result: Mgas=0.048 Msun, Rc=213 au, gamma=0.39 with a good fit
claims.finding: The method works for a bright disk

evidence.quote: Given the simplicity of the model, the overall fit is good with peak residuals less than 10% of the image maximum

claims.hypothesis: The same parameters reproduce the C18O image
claims.finding: Abundance is not strongly radius dependent

evidence.quote: there are no obvious systematics in the difference image suggesting that the abundance does not greatly vary with disk radius.

claims.hypothesis: Profiles of T Tauri disks can be measured economically
claims.experiment: Fit simulated 13CO images across beams and noise levels
claims.result: Rc within about 10 au and gamma within about 0.2 at 0.2-0.3 arcsec
claims.finding: Surveys are feasible with ~20 minute integrations

evidence.quote: we find that we can measure the disk size and gradient parameters to within about $\Delta R_c = 10$ au, $\Delta\gamma = 0.2$.

why_this_method.value: MCMC is too slow with direct radiative transfer, so images are interpolated; zero-moment maps suffice because Keplerian rotation separates regions

evidence.quote: we found that it is not necessary to make tomographic comparisons of channel maps to discriminate between models and that velocity integrated (zero-moment) maps suffice.

limitations_admitted.value: Small errors reflect the rigid imposed temperature structure; allowing it to vary would increase errors

evidence.quote: The apparently high precision obtained here reflects the rigidity of the temperature structure imposed in our models

referee_caveats_inferred: Temperature structure, inclination and stellar mass are fixed, so errors are underestimated
Simulated survey uses idealized noise and circular beams, not uv-plane noise
